newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-TRIP TO ANGOLA SPURRED GUNNELL TO RUN AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-TRIP TO ANGOLA SPURRED GUNNELL TO RUN AGAIN.

text.p: Former Olympic 400-metre hurdles champion Sally Gunnell says the sight of amputees in war-torn Angola persuaded her not to quit athletics despite an acute Achilles tendon injury.

Gunnell, who won Olympic gold in Barcelona in 1992, acknowledged she was very close to announcing her retirement after failing to keep her title last year in Atlanta, where she broke down in the final and had to be carried from the track in agony.
"For the first week it was a case of 'that's it, I've had enough, I can't take any more disappointment'," the former 400-metre hurdles world record holder told Reuters Television in an interview.

"Then I went down to Angola for the Red Cross and I saw people who'd obviously had limbs blown off by landmines and I'm thinking 'hang on a minute, I haven't got a problem here, it's these guys who have got the problem'."
"I think that was a big decision for me to get back on to the track."

Gunnell, speaking at a training centre in Horsham, south-east England, before she left for South Africa to train through the British winter, said she hoped to be back to her best in time for the world championships in Athens in August.
"A little something inside me just thought 'I've got a little more to give'," she said. "I don't want to be remembered for being carried off the track."
